Intelligence needs a decision to serve. Identify the research question, portfolio judgment or investment decision ATRX would inform. Its relevance depends on the choice the institution faces, the horizon over which it matters and the boundaries of its mandate.

Place it within the operating model. Consider who interprets the intelligence, which risk requirements constrain its use and how it enters the existing research workflow. Analytical usefulness alone does not establish operational compatibility.

Keep responsibility explicit. Assumptions, limitations and supporting evidence need to remain open to scrutiny. Establish who reviews the judgment and what would warrant reassessment in the institution’s own environment. Decision authority stays with the institution.

ATRX is designed for systematic allocators, professional trading teams, and enterprise desks that need to interpret complex market conditions together rather than in isolation. Delivered through cloud compute and API distribution, the platform brings institutional market intelligence into existing workflows, supporting consistent research without requiring every organization to build the underlying infrastructure.

Rather than treating price movements as self-explanatory, ATRX examines the economic forces, policy developments, and changing conditions behind market opportunities. Assessments are considered alongside prevailing market conditions and risk controls, preserving context for research and review. Its purpose is to support accountable professional judgment, not promise certainty or replace institutional decision-making authority.
Institutional research must examine the economic transmission, challenge competing explanations, establish where the thesis could fail, and preserve the evidence behind the judgment.
A defensible result can still be unsuitable for a particular institution. The mandate gives the research its decision context.

ATRX organizes market-state observations and systemic economic variables as structured records. Each record describes one instrument vector at a stated time. Read it as of that time: the fields hold what was known then, and the objective resolves only after the evaluation horizon.

Build models, decision rules and research workflows on ATRX records in the language and framework your desk already uses. The aim is a forward-looking judgment the desk can defend: a signal, a classification or a position view that rests on an economic mechanism rather than co-movement alone.

As new market state arrives, ATRX moves it through perception, synthesis, state gating and control. A directive that clears them reaches your endpoint as a signed, schema-validated payload. Your environment verifies it, keeps it, applies desk mandates and only then hands it to your risk engine.

Outputs are judged after the fact, over a review window the desk sets. Realized results are grouped by the regime and structure each payload carried, and ledger exports show what controls stopped, so a review covers decisions that never traded as well as those that did. Findings return to research and shape the next cycle.

ATRX serves systematic allocators, hedge fund and asset management teams, institutional trading desks and qualified quantitative prosumers. Teams use it to evaluate market regimes and macroeconomic transmission within their own risk mandates. See Use cases.

Access is granted by application during ATRX’s closed deployment phase. Engineering reviews each application against compute capacity and infrastructure alignment, and pricing follows technical qualification. Enterprise engagements complete an architecture sync and paper-trading parallel run before live capital. Submit an application.

Prosumer Node serves qualified individual market participants. Capital Desk supports institutional trading teams requiring broader integration and allocation capabilities. Institutional is designed for organizations requiring dedicated infrastructure and governance. See Explore for the full comparison.

Each access mode offers two or three plans on Explore. Select a mode to review its plans and apply from the relevant card; plan allocations are provisional and confirmed during technical qualification.

ATRX provides market regime classification, transition probabilities, structural break detection, macro event impact analysis and causal factor attribution, with cross-asset transmission analysis in Capital Desk and Institutional. Every output is grounded in economic transmission mechanisms rather than correlation alone. See Systemic Macro Intelligence.

Developed FX and Precious Metals were live-traded during Phase 1 validation. Broader currency baskets, equity index topologies and energy vectors are in preparation for v4.0 activation without a published release date, while single-name equities, sovereign rates and volatility remain planned. See Market Coverage.

Outputs are evaluated post-trade across desk-defined review windows, grouping realized results by regime tag and structural identifier alongside decisions halted by risk controls. Methodology and out-of-sample ablation studies are documented in the whitepaper. See Phase 1 performance.

No—across the standard access modes, ATRX is non-custodial and delivers directives to your endpoint while you retain control over API keys, sizing, brokerage execution and counterparty risk. A separate Capital Allocation Partner mandate under negotiated limits is available through Enterprise tenancy.

ATRX delivers signed, schema-validated JSON payloads via webhooks and REST API across all modes, with streaming delivery and low-latency execution SDKs in Capital Desk and Institutional. OMS/EMS connectivity is in development and FIX protocol support is planned. See Quickstart.

Every directive passes through regime gating and the Control protocol, which vetoes exposure breaches and known failure vectors before tenant-side drawdown limits, exposure caps and macro blackout windows apply. These controls govern system behavior and are not a guarantee against loss. See Risk & Control.

ATRX deploys as a single-tenant pipeline (Prosumer Node), a multi-node cohort architecture (Capital Desk) or a dedicated AWS or GCP inference cluster (Institutional). Credentials remain inside the tenant environment, and enterprise deployments validate latency and slippage in paper trading first.

Yes. Institutional provides a dedicated AWS or GCP inference cluster with custom structural modeling and direct engineering support. Private cloud or network connectivity, regional placement and contractual service levels are scoped during technical qualification. See Institutional.

All modes enforce multi-factor authentication, tenant permissions, IP allowlisting, encryption and credential rotation; role-based access control is in development and single sign-on is planned. Decision logs and risk vetoes export in machine-readable formats, with audit-grade telemetry in Institutional (describing record completeness, not regulatory certification). See Audit-Grade Ledgers.

Commercial terms are shared after technical qualification: a monthly compute fee for Prosumer Node, base plus capacity for Capital Desk, and custom terms for Institutional. Admission remains subject to available compute capacity.

Submit an Institutional application outlining your deployment scope, infrastructure environment, integration requirements and governance objectives. Qualified engagements proceed directly to an engineering architecture review.

Visit Documentation for system architecture, methodology, Phase 1 validation metrics and risk disclosures, or Quickstart for payload integration. Full whitepaper and ablation study PDFs are available via documentation request.
Submit access or documentation inquiries through the contact page, or email contact@haldane.xyz for direct technical questions.

passages.text: Every execution payload carries a regime tag and a structural identifier. These give desks a way to attribute realized P&L back to the macroeconomic catalysts and volatility states associated with execution.

Structural identifier. Identifies the structural context carried by the same payload. The example combines it with the regime tag rather than reducing all fills to one aggregate result.
Realized P&L. The desk’s fill records supply realized P&L. The tenant-side example accumulates those values for each regime-and-structure pair over a selected period.

The example groups fills for a month and prints the resulting totals. The period is an example query, not a reporting cadence or a claim about returns. Field names and the payload schema remain onboarding details.
This is a way to organize observed P&L using the context attached to decisions. It does not publish a new causal-estimation methodology or establish that a grouped result alone proves causation.
For the wider decision record, use Audit-Grade Ledgers. Those exports include state classifications and risk veto events as well as decision logs, supporting review beyond filled executions.

Market Intelligence describes the economic-transmission requirement behind execution. Regime & State Analysis describes the gate that responds to conditions. Market context. Multidimensional market-state data and systemic economic variables provide the input context. The task is to interpret the environment in which an opportunity would operate.
Economic transmission. Structural synthesis isolates underlying market drivers. The causal mandate requires an economic transmission mechanism behind execution, beyond historical co-movement.
Structural viability. Inference routing evaluates the viability of the structure and informs capital deployment. A broken causal baseline prevents the strategy from proceeding to execution.

title: Native Risk Mandates

passages.text: The execution node respects daily drawdown limits, exposure caps and macroeconomic blackout windows. Your desk sets the operating constraints; mandates apply them within the execution workflow.
Drawdown thresholds. Daily drawdown limits form part of the desk mandate. The approved example reads the limit from the desk’s own configuration rather than publishing a default percentage.
Exposure limits. An exposure cap constrains deployment. Gross exposure and lot sizing remain under desk control; the example applies a desk-set sizing scalar after its checks.
Blackout windows. Macroeconomic blackout windows are checked before the example evaluates mandate limits. A request inside a window returns a veto instead of proceeding to sizing.
Instrument permissions. The desk retains instrument permissions. The illustrative mandate includes MET_SAFE and FX_DM; the example is not a complete tenant configuration or an availability contract.

The pattern checks for a macro blackout first, then delegates limit evaluation to the illustrative helper. A failed check returns a veto; otherwise the payload passes to sizing with the desk’s lot scalar. Helper behavior and field names are deliberately abstract.

This tenant-side pattern complements ATRX’s systemic Control protocol, which retains veto power over exposure and structural limits. Tier I includes API-level systemic guardrails; Tier II adds custom regime gating and drawdown parameterization.

Exported risk veto events, state classifications and decision logs provide material for internal quantitative review. The ledger examples show one way to inspect the recorded vetoes and observed states.

Policy enforcement is an operational capability, not a regulatory certification or a guarantee of capital preservation. Read it alongside the broader Risk & Control framework and the existing risk disclosure.

title: Structural Philosophy
summary: Why ATRX requires an economic transmission mechanism rather than historical correlation, and how it responds to alpha decay.

passages.text: Rigorous quantitative research and execution infrastructure has largely been available only to firms able to fund it internally. ATRX is built on the premise that the same causal methodology, risk discipline and low-latency delivery can be provided to qualified allocators and desks as shared infrastructure, without lowering the standard.

ATRX delivers causal market intelligence and execution infrastructure to systematic allocators, independent quantitative traders and enterprise desks. It reaches them through cloud compute and API distribution, inside the research, risk and execution environments they already operate.

ATRX is designed to adapt as the markets it models change. Closed-loop telemetry records each execution outcome, and localized failures are logged to a structural ledger that informs the decision stack. When the current market state matches a known failure vector, the Control protocol enforces a hard stop. The objective is to reduce repeated contextual errors as market structure shifts, not to claim immunity from them.

ATRX treats historical correlation as insufficient evidence. Models that rely on co-movement tend to fail at regime shifts, when the relationships they were fitted to break down. Under the Causal Transmission Architecture, every execution must be mapped to an economic transmission mechanism. A strategy does not proceed to execution if its causal baseline is broken, however strong its historical backtest.

An edge begins to decay once it is identified and traded. Many firms respond by adding research capacity. ATRX responds through structural adaptation: perception models map new causal chains as market structure changes, and the inference routing layer reassesses capital deployment as those structures shift.

ATRX models are built as a deterministic computational graph whose decisions can be traced and examined, rather than as an opaque predictive system. Synthesis topologies and regime gates are designed for auditability: decision logs, state classifications and risk veto events are recorded for review.

ATRX is intended to show that institutional-standard quantitative infrastructure can operate outside the traditional fund structure, and that broader access need not come at the expense of methodological rigor or risk discipline.

title: System Architecture
summary: ATRX v4.0: seven structural pillars, a five-stage inference pipeline, and one absolute veto.

headings.text: Seven pillars. Five stages. One absolute veto.

passages.text: Data Ingestion. Continuous aggregation of multidimensional market state data and systemic economic variables.
Structural Topology. A multi-node processing matrix that isolates underlying market drivers without relying on standard historical correlation.
Inference Routing. A dynamic routing layer that evaluates structural viability and informs capital deployment.
State Gating. A multidimensional estimation model that dynamically restricts or permits execution based on prevailing market regimes.
Capital Protection. A strict systemic risk protocol that enforces absolute veto power to maintain mandated exposure and structural limits.
Latency Terminal. Venue-independent protocol adapters translating internal intelligence directives into secure, low-latency market execution.
Telemetry Loop. Every closed loop generates a signed log, embedding localized failures back into the system's structural memory.
Whitepaper summary · v4.0

ATRX v4.0 is organized across seven infrastructural pillars, executed through a deterministic five-stage pipeline, linked to tenant environments via zero-latency webhooks, and refined continuously by a telemetry memory loop. The summary below outlines the computational topology without exposing the proprietary node weights.

Data flows linearly through Perception, Synthesis, Conditioning, and Control before reaching Execution. The Control layer receives a mandatory handoff. If the current market state matches a known failure vector, the protocol enforces a hard stop.

Subscribers map a local endpoint that receives a schema-validated JSON payload from the ATRX intelligence cloud. Execution directives are low-latency and replay-protected, and user credentials never leave the tenant environment.

The architecture runs on natively compiled runtime environments and optimized compute frameworks. The full stack, from the core computational graph to runtime telemetry, is developed in-house and driven by ATRX's own internally developed model.

Currently in active R&D: we are advancing our systemic architecture to extend beyond trade execution, developing autonomous portfolio management frameworks capable of dynamic, multi-strategy capital allocation.

passages.text: ATRX is designed for systematic allocators, professional trading teams and enterprise desks that need to interpret complex market conditions together rather than in isolation. Each team below brings a different question and a different operating environment; in every case, decision and capital authority remain with the team.

Systematic and macro strategies need to know whether a structural opportunity holds under prevailing conditions before capital moves. ATRX evaluates the economic mechanism behind a market move, classifies the regime and delivers an execution payload that the fund’s environment verifies and passes through its own mandates before its risk engine.
Regime awareness. State gating restricts or permits execution according to prevailing market regimes, and the classification travels with the payload. See Regime & State Analysis.
Attribution. Each payload carries a regime tag and a structural identifier, so realized P&L can be attributed to the conditions it was taken in. See Causal Attribution.

An allocation decision depends on a judgment the institution can defend: the mechanism behind a move, where the thesis could fail and how it bears on the mandate. ATRX supports that research and keeps the evidence and reasoning available for review. It does not promise certainty or replace institutional decision-making authority.
Macro research. ATRX connects market-state observations to underlying economic drivers and evaluates whether a causal structure supports capital deployment. See Systemic Macro Intelligence.
Decision support. Prepared briefs set out their assumptions and evidence so they can be compared before the next review. See ATRX in practice.

title: Risk Disclosure
summary: Systematic execution carries inherent structural risk. Disclosures governing deployment of the ATRX intelligence architecture.

headings.text: Systematic execution carries inherent structural risk.

passages.text: The disclosures below govern the deployment of the ATRX intelligence architecture across all tenant endpoints and capital environments.

ATRX deploys deterministic quantitative models that carry inherent risk, including the potential for loss of principal capital. This disclosure outlines the specific mechanical and market-driven risks associated with autonomous execution.

Historical Validation. Performance metrics documented during the Q1 2026 validation window represent past execution data. Documented historical performance does not guarantee future operational yield. Market conditions, structural regime decay, and execution friction will materially impact forward returns.

Algorithmic & Causal Risk. While the architecture utilizes formal methodologies to suppress spurious correlation, algorithmic systems are subject to model misspecification, unanticipated macroeconomic shocks, and data feed latency. Interventional logic cannot perfectly predict market reflexivity.

Execution & Counterparty. ATRX computes intelligence; it does not custody capital. The tenant assumes all counterparty risk associated with their chosen brokerage or liquidity provider. ATRX is not liable for broker insolvency, API downtime, spread widening, or slippage incurred during high-volatility regime shifts.

Jurisdictional Governance. The deployment of automated trading pipelines is subject to varied global regulation. Enterprise tenants are strictly responsible for ensuring their use of the ATRX SDK complies with local financial law, capital reporting, and tax obligations.

System Capacity. ATRX provides execution payloads and topological research. It does not provide individualized financial advice or guarantee capital preservation. Tenants retain ultimate discretionary authority over their API keys and capital deployment sizing.
